true: The paper studies world models, world simulators, or learned dynamics models for embodied, robotic, or physical agents. This includes: video generation or diffusion used for world simulation; JEPA-style predictive or joint-embedding architectures; latent dynamics or latent action models; embodied or physical AI; VLA / vision-language-action policies built on predictive or world models; and evaluation, benchmarks, or efficiency work (acceleration, distillation, quantization, real-time inference, memory reduction) on any of the above. It also includes work that supports this area even when the phrase "world model" never appears: synthetic or generated training data for robot or embodied learning (demonstration synthesis, trajectory or interaction data generation, sim-ready scene generation, scalable robot datasets); long-horizon memory for video or embodied agents, including memory compression, memory distillation, and compact memory architectures; and datasets, benchmarks, or evaluation protocols for embodied, robotic, or physical tasks such as manipulation, navigation, and physical interaction.
false: The paper is outside this scope: it does not study world models, learned dynamics or simulators, robot or embodied data and benchmarks, or long-horizon memory for video and embodied agents. Examples: pure NLP or speech, medical or clinical work, security or code generation, networking or wireless sensing, generic 3D reconstruction or image restoration, and video work with no world-model, memory, or embodied component.
